name: NJ-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Rob Menendez running with a large fundraising edge
No Republican on the ballot; independents stand in opposition
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 95%
model.rationale: The seat's D+15 lean, Menendez's incumbency and roughly $2 million raised against opponents with no visible fundraising, and Polymarket pricing near 95% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold. With no Republican on the ballot and no polling, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which remain firmly favorable.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or major outside spending against Menendez could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Aristotle Eliopoulos is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Rob Menendez, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a northern New Jersey district that leans Democratic by about 15 points. He has raised nearly $2 million and holds a large cash advantage, while the candidates opposing him are independents with no reported fundraising. No Republican appears on the general-election ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 95%. The seat is expected to remain in Democratic hands by a wide margin, though the absence of polling leaves some room for error.
